## TSLA — Technical Analysis Report
**Instrument:** Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) · NMS · Consumer Cyclical / Auto Manufacturers
**As of:** 2026-10-26 (close) · **Verified close:** $391.62

---

# 1. Executive Summary

TSLA closed at **$391.62** on 2026-10-26, **+5.21%** on the session (prior close $372.22), on volume of **52,672,239** shares. The close is the **highest since 2026-07-01 ($425.30)** and the intraday high of **$397.27** is the **highest print since 2026-07-15 ($406.59)**.

The technical picture flipped decisively bullish today, and — importantly — it did so on *multiple independent axes* simultaneously:

1. **First close above the falling 200-day SMA** ($386.13) — every close from 2026-08-27 through 2026-10-23 was below that line.
2. **A fresh MACD bull crossover** — MACD line 3.98 crossed above its signal line 3.01, with the histogram jumping from **-0.13 (10-23) to +0.97 (10-26)**.
3. **RSI re-accelerated** from 42.20 (10-16) to **60.10** — bullish momentum, still well below the 70 overbought line.
4. **Price is above the VWMA** ($374.36) by 4.6%, and the VWMA itself is in a persistent uptrend — volume-weighted accumulation is confirmed, not speculative.

The one cautionary note: the close came back **below the upper Bollinger band** ($393.76) after piercing it intraday ($397.27), and the 10-26 bar gave back roughly a third of its high-to-low range from the top. Also, the 200-day SMA is still *declining* (~-0.3 points/session), so this is a **trend-transition bar, not a confirmed regime change**.

**Working bias: cautiously bullish / buy-the-dip-and-breakout hybrid.** Add on a successful retest of the 200 SMA ($386.13) or on a volume-confirmed break of $397.27. Do not chase an extended move into $400–402 without confirmation.

---

# 2. Indicator Selection & Rationale (8 indicators)

The market condition here is a **high-volatility single-name in the middle of a trend transition** — a basing/reversal tape after a multi-month decline (2025-12-16 peak close $489.88 → 2026-07-23 low close $319.69, a ~34.6% drawdown) with violent single-day gap risk. The selection prioritizes *trend hierarchy* (three horizons), *momentum inflection*, *volume confirmation*, and *volatility-normalized risk*.

| # | Indicator | Category | Why it's included (non-redundant role) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `close_10_ema` | Moving Avg | Fast tactical trend/entry-timing filter; defines the "line in the sand" for short-term momentum |
| 2 | `close_50_sma` | Moving Avg | Medium-term trend + dynamic support; quantifies the constructive bias and anchors the 2-ATR stop |
| 3 | `close_200_sma` | Moving Avg | Long-term regime benchmark; the pivotal level TSLA just reclaimed — and the only thing that distinguishes a bounce from a reversal |
| 4 | `macd` | MACD | Absolute trend momentum (above/below zero) and the direction of the underlying EMA spread |
| 5 | `macdh` | MACD | *Acceleration* — the histogram's turn from -2.43 (10-01) to +0.97 (10-26) is the earliest, most sensitive momentum tell; catches inflection before the level-based signals |
| 6 | `rsi` | Momentum | Normalized momentum regime + overbought/oversold context; confirms price action isn't diverging from the move |
| 7 | `atr` | Volatility | Converts levels into risk: stop distance, position sizing, and a realistic sense of daily noise (3.44% of price) |
| 8 | `vwma` | Volume | Volume-weighted trend confirmation — separates genuine institutional accumulation from price that drifts on thin participation |

**Deliberately excluded (redundancy control):**
- `macds` — the signal line is already fully expressed through `macdh` (MACD 3.98 − signal 3.01 = 0.97 ✓). Pulling it in would duplicate information.
- `boll` (middle) — a 20-day SMA; largely redundant with the 50/200 SMAs already in the stack for trend purposes.
- `boll_ub` / `boll_lb` — used in this report as *supplementary context* drawn from the verified snapshot (not counted in the 8), because a single band without the others is less informative; the band complex is referenced primarily to define the immediate upside magnet at $393.76 and the volatility envelope.

---

# 3. Price Action & Multi-Scale Trend Structure

### 3.1 The dominant context: a 34.6% drawdown being repaired
From the **2025-12-16 peak close of $489.88** to the **2026-07-23 low close of $319.69**, TSLA lost ~34.6%. From that low, the stock has recovered **+22.50%** to $391.62. Today's close is still **-20.05%** below the December peak and roughly **-9.7%** below the 2025-10-24 close of $433.72 (one year ago).

So the current move is a **counter-trend rally within a still-damaged long-term structure** — until and unless the 200 SMA flattens and turns up, the rally remains a *recovery* trade rather than a *new uptrend* trade.

### 3.2 Three-horizon trend alignment (the most important read in this report)

| Horizon | Value (2026-10-26) | Slope | Price position | Read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 EMA | $376.09 | Rising (from $352.00 on 09-01) | Price **+4.13% above** | Short-term constructive |
| 50 SMA | $364.76 | Rising (from $346.57 on 10-01, +$18.19 in 18 sessions) | Price **+7.36% above** | Intermediate constructive |
| 200 SMA | $386.13 | **Falling** (from $401.41 on 08-27, -$15.28) | Price **+1.42% above** | Long-term still bearish, but reclaimed |

**Key finding — the 50/200 relationship:** The 50 SMA ($364.76) is still **$21.37 below** the 200 SMA ($386.13) — a death-cross configuration. However, the gap has collapsed from **$45.60 on 2026-10-02** ($393.18 − $347.58) to **$21.37 today**, an approximate halving in 18 sessions. At the recent slope (50 SMA rising ~+$0.33/session, 200 SMA declining ~-$0.29/session, i.e. ~$0.62/session of convergence), the two averages would meet in roughly **5–7 weeks (early December 2026)** *if* TSLA holds above ~$390 and the averages keep their current drift. Flattening or a pullback to the $365–375 zone would stall that clock significantly. This is a *conditional projection*, not a scheduled event.

**Key finding — the 200 SMA reclaim is real, not cosmetic:** Cross-checking the closes against the 200 SMA values from the indicator series: 09-03 close $376.37 vs 200 SMA $399.83; 09-23 close $380.12 vs $396.34; 10-06 close $380.68 vs $392.19; 10-09 close $382.70 vs $390.60; and notably **10-21 close $386.47 vs $386.94** — a hair below. Every close from 2026-08-27 through 2026-10-23 was beneath the 200 SMA. **Today's $391.62 is the first close above it in that window.** The very near-miss on 10-21 and today's decisive clearance make $386.13 the single most consequential level on the chart.

### 3.3 The short-term base and today's bar
- Recent swing low: **2026-10-16**, low $349.33 / close $354.72 (following the 09-29 close low of $352.84).
- The stock rallied **+10.4% from the 10-16 close** ($354.72 → $391.62) in seven sessions, with the heaviest single-day thrust today.
- **10-26 bar anatomy:** Open $383.97 (just $0.13 above the low $383.84), High $397.27, Low $383.84, Close $391.62. The open sat on the low and the close finished in the **upper 58% of the day's 13.43-point range** — a bullish "auction from the low" shape. But the close is **$5.65 (1.45%) below the high**, indicating real supply met at $397.27, and the day's range ($13.43) is essentially exactly **1.0× ATR** — this was a full-range volatility expansion day, not a low-conviction grind.

### 3.4 Volume profile — a genuine participation event
Comparing the 18 October sessions (10-01 through 10-26), the average volume is roughly **37.0M shares**. Today's **52,672,239** is about **1.42× that average**, and it sits in the upper tier of the recent range (vs. 62.07M on the 10-16 selloff and 51.61M on 10-22). **Caveat:** the 10-26 volume figure (52,672,239) has non-standard precision compared with the round figures in the surrounding series, which may indicate a partial-session or provisional print. Treat the volume confirmation as *likely valid but provisional*, and re-verify at the next session's data.

# 4. Momentum Analysis

### 4.1 MACD — a genuine cross, not a whipsaw artifact
MACD line **3.98**, signal **3.01**, histogram **+0.97**. The sequence is textbook and worth tracing:

| Date | MACD | Histogram | Event |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-24 | 6.64 | +1.63 | Momentum high |
| 2026-10-01 | 1.28 | **-2.43** | Momentum trough |
| 2026-10-16 | 1.41 | **-2.09** | Secondary trough (with price low) |
| 2026-10-19 | 1.27 | -1.79 | Cross back up |
| 2026-10-21 | 2.85 | +0.07 | Marginal bull cross |
| 2026-10-23 | 2.64 | **-0.13** | Cross *failed* — mini divergence |
| 2026-10-26 | **3.98** | **+0.97** | Decisive re-cross, largest positive since 2026-09-25 |

**Interpretation:** The 10-21 cross was not yet a valid signal — it was negated within two sessions (10-23 histogram -0.13). What makes today's cross credible is *confirmation*: it arrives with the MACD line at its highest level since 2026-10-09 ($5.07) trending up from a $1.27 base, **above the zero line**, alongside a fresh 200 SMA reclaim and RSI expansion. The histogram's +0.97 is the largest positive reading since 2026-09-25 (+1.08), indicating **momentum acceleration rather than mere continuation**.

**Caution:** MACD has been whipsawing violently in this regime — the histogram crossed zero four times between 2026-09-15 and 2026-10-26 (sign flips on 09-16, 09-18, 10-02, 10-05, 10-13, 10-21, 10-23, 10-26). MACD signals in TSLA at this volatility regime deserve a 2–3 session confirmation rule, not one-day action.

### 4.2 RSI — bullish, not stretched
RSI **60.10**, up from **42.20** on 2026-10-16 (the local RSI trough) and 51.52 on 10-23.

- **No overbought condition.** At 60, RSI leaves ~10 points of runway before the conventional 70 threshold.
- **No bearish divergence.** The 10-21 close of $386.47 came with RSI 59.77; today's higher close of $391.62 carries RSI 60.10 — RSI is marginally *higher* on a higher price. Momentum is confirming price, not diverging.
- **Historical context in this tape:** RSI spent early-to-mid September pinned in the 50–60 band while price chopped between roughly $353 and $380 — a coil. RSI's break to 60.10 today resolves that range to the upside.
- **Watch for:** an RSI failure back below ~50 (which would signal the 10-23-style mini-cross failure repeating) versus a push through 65–70, which combined with a close above the upper Bollinger band would signal a short-term exhaustion zone.

---

# 5. Volume Confirmation (VWMA)

VWMA = **$374.36**, rising from **$344.40 on 2026-08-27** (+8.7% over two months) — a clean, persistent upward slope with no rollover.

- Price at $391.62 sits **+4.61% above the VWMA**. In a healthy uptrend, price trades a modest premium to the volume-weighted average; a *large* premium (as now) with the VWMA still rising is the signature of **demand absorbing supply**, not a blow-off.
- Cross-check: the 10 EMA ($376.09) and VWMA ($374.36) are converging tightly (0.46% apart) at the $374–376 shelf. This is now a **well-defined dynamic support zone** — the first line where the trend would be questioned.
- A VWMA flattening/turning down while price holds above it would be the classic warning that distribution is beginning to outweigh demand.

---

# 6. Volatility & Risk (ATR)

ATR = **$13.47**, or **3.44% of the close**. ATR has expanded ~22% in two weeks (from $11.04 on 2026-10-13 to $13.47 on 10-26) — volatility is *rising into* the breakout, which is normal for a trend transition but must be respected in position sizing.

**ATR-derived levels (arithmetically direct from the verified values):**

| Reference | Calculation | Level |
|---|---|---|
| 1× ATR below close | 391.62 − 13.47 | **$378.15** |
| 1.5× ATR below close | 391.62 − 20.20 | **$371.42** |
| 2× ATR below close | 391.62 − 26.94 | **$364.68** ≈ 50 SMA $364.76 |

**Notable confluence:** a standard 2-ATR stop from the current close lands at **$364.68**, essentially *exactly* on the 50-day SMA ($364.76). This is a genuinely useful coincidence — it means the 50 SMA and an ATR-based maximum-risk stop are the same place. Stops placed at the 50 SMA are, by construction, a 2-ATR risk from here.

**Gap risk that ATR cannot capture (critical for TSLA):** ATR measures *intraday* range and is blind to overnight gaps. On **2026-07-23**, TSLA gapped from a $374.01 close to a $341.00 open and closed at **$319.69 (−14.5%)** on **115,606,400 shares** — roughly 2.2× today's volume. A stop-loss at $364 would have executed nowhere near $364 in that scenario. **Stops alone are not risk control in this name.** Use reduced position sizing and/or defined-risk options (call spreads on continuation, put spreads on failure) rather than relying on a hard stop alone.

---

# 8. Actionable Trade Plans

### Plan A — Breakout continuation (primary)
- **Trigger:** a close **above $397.27** (today's high) on volume > ~45M shares (above the ~37M 18-session October average), with the close holding above the $393.76 upper Bollinger band.
- **Entry:** on the break, or on a successful retest of $397 as support.
- **Targets:** $398.73–$401.68 (first, near-term magnet — also the May 5/6 congestion) → $409.28 → $415.83–$419.77.
- **Stop:** $378.15 (1× ATR) for an intraday trade; $371.42 (1.5× ATR) for a swing. Hard invalidation: a close back below **$386.13**, which would void the 200 SMA reclaim.
- **R/R:** to $409 from a $398 entry with a $378 stop ≈ 2.8:1. Acceptable.

### Plan B — Retest buy (preferred risk/reward)
- **Trigger:** a pullback into the **$383–$388** band (today's low/open zone + 200 SMA at $386.13) that produces a bullish rejection candle and holds **above $386.13 on a closing basis**.
- **Entry:** on the reclaim of $388–390 after a confirmed hold of the 200 SMA.
- **Deeper entry:** the **$371–376** shelf (Bollinger mid $371.58 / VWMA $374.36 / 10 EMA $376.09) if the 200 SMA retest fails and price stabilizes.
- **Stop:** below $364.68 (2× ATR ≈ 50 SMA) for the deep case; below $371.42 for the shallow case.
- **Note:** Plan B offers materially better R/R than chasing $391.62 with the upper band $2.14 overhead.

### Plan C — Failed reclaim (bearish contingency, lower probability)
- **Trigger:** a close back **below $386.13** followed by a failed attempt to reclaim it within 1–2 sessions, with MACD histogram re-turning negative and RSI failing back below ~50.
- **Targets:** $376.09 (10 EMA) → $371.58 → $364.76 (50 SMA) → $354.72.
- **Stop:** above $397.27.
- **Framing:** with MACD freshly crossed, RSI at 60, price above the VWMA and the 50 SMA rising, this is a *lower-probability* scenario. The correct response to it is primarily **"do not add / tighten stops,"** not "short."

### Positioning discipline
1. **Scale in, don't sprint.** The 200 SMA is a declining line; a single close above it is a *signal*, not a confirmed regime change. Half-size on the first reclaim, add on the retest.
2. **Size by ATR, not by conviction.** With ATR at $13.47 (3.44% of price) and a demonstrated 14.5% single-day gap risk (2026-07-23), cap risk per idea at a level that survives a gap through your stop.
3. **The $386.13 line is the thesis.** Long while it holds on a closing basis; reduce when it fails; exit short-term exposure if the close slips below $374–376 (10 EMA + VWMA) with a negative MACD histogram.
4. **Watch the calendar, not just the chart.** TSLA's earnings-style event risk is the single largest gap risk in this name; a 1.5–2 ATR cushion is not adequate protection through a catalyst.

## TSLA — Sentiment Report, 2026-10-19 → 2026-10-26

**Headline read:** Sentiment around TSLA is directionally positive but unevenly distributed. Institutional/news framing and the X/robotaxi-tracking cohort are outright bullish; the fast-moving retail tape (StockTwits) is close to flat-to-mildly-bullish with heavy two-sided options hedging; Reddit shows a mixed picture dominated by realized retail losses and merger-arbitrage speculation rather than conviction. Net: bullish momentum narrative, but the crowd is paying up and hedging at the same time.

---

### 1. Source-by-source breakdown

**News (Yahoo Finance headlines, 20 items — 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-26)**
Roughly 13–14 headlines are TSLA-supportive, 4–5 are cautionary/relative-value, and 3 are essentially off-theme noise (Musk net-worth musings, the Audi CEO/Trump rally backlash story, the Skydance/Roku item).

- *Bullish core:* "Tesla Stock Soars on Wave of Analyst Upgrades"; "Tesla Stocks Rise 5.34% After Barclays Lifts Target to $450"; "Barclays Makes Bold Tesla Stock Call After SpaceX Twist"; "SpaceX Merger Could Accelerate Tesla's Push Into AI and Autonomous Driving: Barclays"; "Tesla Stock Leaves Rest of the Magnificent 7 in the Dust, Surging to October's Top Spot"; "Tesla Cybercabs Could Reach Customers by End of 2026"; "Tesla's Full Self-Driving Business Is Growing Fast"; "Musk: Terafab Will Rank in 'Top 20' GDP From a Single Building."
- *Institutional/operational:* "Fort Bend County sweetens pot to land $10B Tesla solar plant" — a real-economy capacity commitment, though it also underlines that Tesla's growth capital is going into energy/manufacturing build-outs rather than equity returns.
- *Counter-framing:* "Move Over, Tesla: This Robotics Stock Is the Better Buy" (Motley Fool relative-value); "Tesla's Full Self-Driving Business Is Growing Fast. But There's a Catch for Investors" (monetization caveat attached to the same headline that otherwise reads bullish); "This Bearish Spread Will Pay Off If Tesla Stock Trends Lower" (IBD — an explicitly constructed bearish options position); and the Scott Galloway line ("Tesla's the Patient and SpaceX Is the Organ Donor"), which is a jab at the *pace* of Tesla's payoff relative to SpaceX.
- *Built-in caveat in Musk's own framing:* Cybercabs reaching customers by end-2026 "but the vast majority will be TSLA-owned" — that is a fleet-asset story (capex, depreciation) rather than a third-party revenue story, and the market is only partly pricing that distinction.

Institutional framing here is unambiguous: an upgrade cycle with a $450 Barclays target, and TSLA as the strongest Mag 7 name of the month.

**StockTwits (23 on-topic messages; screener stance read 7 bullish / 6 bearish / 5 neutral / 5 unclear)**
Tagged messages run 6 bullish (26%) vs 4 bearish (17%), with 13 of 23 unlabeled (57%) — so the "labeled" ratio is ~60/40 for bulls, but the full classified set is essentially 50/50. On a 23-message sample with only 10 explicit tags, this is a weak-to-moderate bullish signal at best.

What the messages actually show is *two-sided options positioning around a breakout*:
- Bullish: "420 soon"; "Thanks $TSLA, you were a good hold over the weekend"; bare "TSLA" + checkmark posts; one post noting 386–389 "stopped it five times since Sep 23" and that it "went straight through, tagged 397 and closed 391."
- Bearish/hedging: "my puts are looking good"; "$SPY $TSLA Deep red week coming — I've got my puts"; "$TSLA lets see how far this after hr drop can go. Should atleast get to 384"; "Back fill tomorrow?"; "Fugly close."
- Neutral/uncertain: "I'll see how it handles lows tomorrow"; "What level would flip you back to bullish?"; the heaviest-volume strike note — **Oct 30 $400 calls, 29,000+ contracts, largest single-strike volume on the board** — explicitly flagged as ambiguous ("somebody may be loading up – or unwinding," open interest confirmation due pre-market).
- Persistent retail pain: "$TSLA I had 20 $380 calls expire worthless on Friday" and "I was so close with that 185 put" — a pattern of short-dated premium decay, i.e., the fast-money cohort is being worn down rather than accumulating.
- One politically charged post is pure noise and carries no directional signal.
- Useful context from a regime tracker: TSLA is currently in a **"Mildly Off" regime where its typical 3-month return is −1.2% (up only 46% of the time)**, versus +15.9% (up 64%) in Risk-On regimes. That is a caution against extrapolating the current risk-on melt-up.
